children: Nearly three decades of experience across power, mining, infrastructure and finance leadership roles in India shape his new mandate today

Dr. Prasanna Kumar Acharya has taken charge as Chairman-cum-Managing Director (CMD) of NLC India, succeeding to the top leadership position at the energy and mining company. He assumed office on 17 September 2026 at the company’s Corporate Office in Neyveli.

Acharya brings nearly three decades of professional experience across the power, mining and infrastructure sectors. Before taking charge as CMD, he served as Director (Finance) at NLC India, giving him experience of the company’s financial operations and business activities.

Acharya’s professional career includes senior roles at GRIDCO, NTPC, Tata Power and NLC India. His experience spans power generation, transmission and distribution, mining and metro rail infrastructure.

His career has included responsibilities across different segments of the energy and infrastructure ecosystem, along with senior finance functions. His previous role as Director (Finance) at NLC India provided exposure to the company’s financial and operational priorities before his elevation to the CMD position.
As Director (Finance), Acharya was part of the senior leadership at NLC India, with responsibilities linked to the company’s financial function.

His wider professional experience includes work across public-sector and private-sector organisations in the power and infrastructure space. The combination of finance experience and sector exposure forms part of his professional background as he takes on the CMD role.
(Honours) from Utkal University and an LLB from M.S. Law College, Cuttack. He also holds a Master of Commerce from Ravenshaw University and an MBA.
His academic background combines commerce, law and management, alongside his professional experience in finance and infrastructure.
NLC India operates across the power and mining value chain, making the CMD position central to the company’s overall management and business direction.

Acharya’s appointment marks a leadership transition at the company, with his previous experience in finance and his broader exposure to power, mining and infrastructure forming the foundation of his new role.
